headline: High: shared filesystem and broad shell/network on slim create dangerous default interaction risks with caveman’s MCP/file-facing workflow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman uses MCP and reads/writes project files like CLAUDE.md and memory files, while slim exposes stdin/stdout and filesystem artifacts. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if slim outputs are copied into caveman’s trusted files or prompts. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF slim output is pasted into caveman-managed prompt or memory files
IF caveman treats file contents as trusted instructions
mitigations: Keep slim output out of CLAUDE.md and memory files
Review copied text before feeding it to caveman
Use separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable MCP access for caveman during untrusted analysis
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while slim reads and writes filesystem artifacts and handles certificate private keys and registry credentials. If they share a workspace, sensitive artifacts can flow from slim into caveman outputs or logs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible from profiles alone, but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory tree
IF slim processes certificate private keys or registry credentials in that workspace
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate workspace
Remove secrets before running caveman
Restrict caveman access to sensitive directories
Rotate any credentials exposed to slim
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and writes project files, while slim has write_filesystem plus execute_shell and spawn_subprocesses. If both target the same directory, concurrent writes can corrupt files or overwrite each other; slim’s broader execution surface makes the conflict more dangerous. No locking is documented, so the safer higher severity is high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path
IF caveman instances run concurrently with slim in one workspace
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories
Serialize writes with a manual lock file
Back up the workspace before execution
Avoid concurrent runs on the same target
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman is a content-writing agent that can produce project notes and CLAUDE.md content, and slim is an interactive CLI that can act on filesystem and shell state. If slim consumes caveman’s output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into incorrect container changes or destructive commands. The pathway exists, but there is no evidence of automatic action chaining.
conditions: IF slim uses caveman-generated text as command input or runbook
IF caveman output is not independently verified before execution
mitigations: Require human review before slim executes instructions
Cross-check caveman outputs against source files
Limit slim to read-only dry runs first
Keep caveman outputs in a separate review folder
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: slim explicitly handles registry credentials, certificate private keys, and vulnerability data, while caveman touches session logs and memory files. If the pair is used on regulated or secret-bearing workloads, retention and residency controls can diverge and create compliance gaps. Only slim is cited for secret handling because the compliance risk is driven by its documented secret-bearing surfaces.
conditions: IF regulated secrets or private keys are processed by slim
IF caveman logs or retains those artifacts in session logs or memory files
mitigations: Exclude regulated secrets from both agents
Shorten log retention for caveman outputs
Run slim only on non-sensitive images
Document data handling boundaries for both tools
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
